name: code-review
description: Unified code review that fans out parallel scanners over a change — one per active lens, up to eleven per run — and merges them into one per-file report. Eleven lenses: comment quality, four quality/craft lenses (readability & tests, naming & module, objects & patterns, simplicity & types), an always-on correctness lens (wrong conditions, unhandled cases, off-by-one, swallowed errors, races, broken call contracts), an always-on narrow security lens (secrets, injection, access checks, boundary validation, insecure settings, IaC exposure, access widening, plus access policies and CI workflows), an always-on coherence lens (docs, contracts, migrations, config and sibling listings that disagree with the code or each other, code breaking a rule an accepted ADR or CONTEXT.md states), an always-on assumptions lens (code relying on library, runtime, CI or platform behaviour the installed source or the locked version contradicts, test doubles the real dependency would not match), a performance lens for executable source (N+1, unbounded fetch, blocking-in-async, wasted renders, missing indexes), and a spec lens via --spec <path> or a spec file the diff carries. Explicit rules in a root CODING_STANDARDS.md (plus a gitignored .local.md overlay) generate standards findings. The standalone comment-review and quality-review skills stay invocable for a single-lens pass. Reviews the current branch diff by default (or explicit paths / --base, or a GitHub PR with --pr). Quality findings are tagged family · rule · severity; comment verdicts are R1–R12 · KEEP/REMOVE/REWRITE/MOVE/ADD, shown side by side and applied through a single risk-cut menu. Successor to the comment-review and quality-review plugins.
